lessons.lessonDescription: Comprehend (in spoken and written language) that the term “partition” refers to splitting a shape into parts. Explain (orally) how to partition shapes into 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 equal parts. Identify (orally and in writing) equal parts as “halves,” “thirds,” “fourths,” “sixths,” and “eighths.”
Comprehend (in spoken language) the meaning of the term “unit fraction.” Generalize (orally) that a fraction \(\frac{a}{b}\) refers to a quantity of \(a\) parts of size \(\frac{1}{b}\) .
Critique (orally) statements and generalizations about fractions, whole numbers represented as fractions, and fraction comparisons.

Comprehend (in spoken and written language) the meaning of the term “fraction,” and that the notation \(\frac{1}{b}\) can be used to represent unit fractions. Draw and label to partition shapes into halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, and eighths. Express the size of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
Determine (orally and in writing) estimates of fractions represented in diagrams and on number lines that are “too low,” “about right,” and “too high.”
Justify (orally) that a non-unit fraction has the same value as a number of unit fractions. Represent (using diagrams) a word problem involving non-unit fractions.
